rationale_evidence.anchor: Derivation of Bayes's Theorem: Step 1, by the Ratio Formula cr(H|E)=cr(H^E)/cr(E). Step 2, by the Ratio Formula symmetric, cr(E^H)=cr(E|H)*cr(H). Step 3, since H^E == E^H, cr(H|E)=cr(E|H)*cr(H)/cr(E). ... Certainties are Created: if E is learned between t_i,t_j then cr_j(E)=cr_i(E|E)=1. Certainties are Retained: if cr_i(H)=1 then cr_j(H)=1. Conditionalization is Cumulative: conditionalizing on E then E' equals conditionalizing on E^E'. Conditionalization is Commutative: update on E then E' equals update on E' then E.
rationale_evidence.statement: Reproduces the three-step derivation of Bayes's Theorem from the Ratio Formula, and four derived properties of Conditionalization: certainties are created (learned evidence becomes certain), certainties are retained (once credence 1, always credence 1 under conditionalization), conditionalization is cumulative (sequential conditionalization on E then E' equals conditionalizing on their conjunction), and conditionalization is commutative (update order does not matter) -- all reproduced verbatim from the source.

rationale_evidence.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
rationale_evidence.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

rationale_evidence.anchor: NumberOfAIOutputs \neq AmountOfIndependentEvidence
rationale_evidence.statement: If five LLMs all say 'Nexus is running 3.69', that must NOT be treated as five independent observations, since they may all derive from the same underlying source or from each other: NumberOfAIOutputs ≠ AmountOfIndependentEvidence — exactly why provenance belongs in the model. Worked provenance graph: Primary Source->Artifact A->Observation O1->LLM interpretation->Observation O2->Candidate Assertion A1, then a second LLM consumes A1 to produce A2, so KnowledgeOS can determine 'A2 ultimately depends on A1, which ultimately depends on Artifact A' — far more powerful than a bare confidence=0.93 score. Gives Zero a provenance-analysis role: Zero:ProvenanceAnalysis->EpistemicBoundary, identifying unsupported claims, circular evidence, duplicate evidence, stale/conflicting observations, source dependency, interpretation uncertainty (e.g. flagging 'three supporting AI outputs that all originate from the same source').

rationale_evidence.anchor: EvidenceCount \neq IndependentEvidenceCount
rationale_evidence.statement: Test Case 5 (three LLMs agreeing) shows a naive support count of 3 is wrong if all three derived their answer from the same original document (O_1->LLM_1, O_1->LLM_2, O_1->LLM_3 are not independent evidence): EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount, so provenance is 'mathematically relevant to epistemic assessment', not optional metadata. Test Case 6 (conflicting DB/document/monitoring sources) confirms Conflict is created AFTER semantic interpretation (DetectConflict(P_1,P_2,Rule)->C), not at raw ingestion.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The Sarathi reading hardens into I-1
rationale_evidence.statement: After the crisis, the corpus reorganized itself around numbered questions -- how does knowledge change state, who owns the goal, what makes evidence sufficient -- and, in parallel, returned to the Gita lens with new seriousness. The era's great gift to the final architecture is the Sarathi (charioteer) reading: the Knower owns the frame; everything else serves it. Of all the era's images, this is the one that hardened into an invariant (I-1) and survived every later regime unchanged. When Part III.2 says the Knower owns problem, purpose, IdealState, and final authority, it is speaking the formalized residue of this reading.

rationale_evidence.statement: H-K08 (Guidance ≠ Authority) consequences: formally a 5-way chain (Guidance/Authority/Decision/Execution/Transition) with each boundary separately witnessed.
